name: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026
short_description: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026 is a verified women-only Half Marathon plus family-distance race in Singapore, confirmed for 1 November 2026 with open registration.
ai_summary: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026 is a women-focused road race at Singapore's National Stadium / The Kallang precinct, confirmed for 1 November 2026 with a 4:30am start. Organized by Great Eastern, it centers on a 21.1km women-only Half Marathon alongside 10km and 5km categories, plus family-oriented 2km "Mummy+Me" and 100m "Princess Dash" events. Registration is open directly via the official website, verified as of 20 July 2026.

core_facts.venue: Singapore National Stadium / The Kallang (4:30am start)

pros: Women-only Half Marathon category alongside family-friendly 2km and 100m events broadens participation beyond a typical marathon field
Registration is open directly via the official site, no third-party platform required
cons: Five distinct categories at one event may make choosing the right entry confusing for first-time participants

faqs.question: Is the Great Eastern Women's Run open to men?
faqs.answer: The race's headline 21.1km Half Marathon category is women-only, consistent with the event's name and positioning. The event also includes 10km and 5km categories plus family-oriented 2km and 100m events, so check the official race website directly for each category's specific eligibility rules before registering.

faqs.question: What time does the Great Eastern Women's Run start?
faqs.answer: The race starts early, at 4:30am, from Singapore's National Stadium / The Kallang precinct, confirmed for 1 November 2026. Early starts are common for Singapore road races to avoid the heat and humidity of daytime running, so plan your travel and warm-up time accordingly.

faqs.question: What distances can I run at the Great Eastern Women's Run?
faqs.answer: Five categories are offered: a 21.1km women-only Half Marathon, a 10km, a 5km, a 2km "Mummy+Me" run, and a 100m "Princess Dash" for children. This spread makes the event suitable for competitive runners, casual participants, and families attending together at the same race morning.
